title.narrative: In 2025, UNICEF advanced child-centered climate policy, planning and advocacy in Zimbabwe, contributing to improved resilience of children, young people, and their families to climate change. UNICEF supported the integration of child sensitivity into four national and international climate and environment policy processes, exceeding the annual target. These included the Declaration of Children, Youth and Climate Action, the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0 Country Statement, the National Energy Compact, and the National Climate Change Management Bill, reinforcing a national commitment to putting children at the centre of climate action. Children and young people actively shaped these processes, including contributions by 40 children to NDC 3.0 and 150 young people to the Pre-COP 30 Position Paper, informing future submissions. Evidence generation resulted in one child-sensitive climate vulnerability assessment, while 1,500 young climate advocates were engaged through national and international platforms. Sub-national initiatives further amplified children's voices through environment clubs, experiential learning and structured coordination under the KOICA supported project Climate Action for the Last Mile (CALM).
